intent: Widen the sensor span from ±0.04 m to ±0.06 m (five sensors at 0.03 m spacing), as the Integrator's requested change for persistent line loss with max_error at the limit. Everything else stays fixed, including sensor y = 0.05, so the effect of span can be read directly. Expected result: line_loss_events close to 0, max_error below 0.06 m, and higher progress on the oval and s-bend. Score should rise above 130.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) line losses persist because the ±0.04 m span still does not see the tape beyond about 0.05 m of lateral error, so ±0.06 m should remove them. (2) Max_error sits at the limit because the robot drifts past sensor coverage, not because it oscillates, so a wider span should lower it. (3) Steering oscillation may rise with the wider span. If the oval exceeds 0.25 while losses fall, the next step is sensor y 0.05 to 0.03. If losses are gone but rms_error stays above 0.03, the next step is sensor_size 0.008. Please report per-track values so the slalom (highest max_error, 0.0685) can be checked separately.
rationale: Iteration 1 (sensor span ±0.04 m) scored 129.96, up from 56.86 at ±0.03 m. The gain is real but incomplete. Every run still ended off_track with progress 0.16 to 0.53, line_loss_events stayed at about 1.0 to 1.05 per run, and max_error was 0.062 to 0.069, at or above the 0.06 m off-track limit. The sensor footprint still does not cover the drift far enough out. The Integrator's rule for this case is to widen the span to ±0.06 at 0.03 m spacing. Steering oscillation is 0.22 to 0.27 by track (mean about 0.24), so the sensor-lead reduction is not yet triggered on average. The oval alone (0.275) is above the 0.25 threshold, and I will watch it, but I am not changing sensor y in the same step so that the span change can be attributed cleanly. rms_error (0.024 to 0.031) is not the limiting factor, so sensor_size stays at 0.012. body_width stays at 0.12 because the off-track limit is already at its floor and cannot help. I expect line_loss_events to fall toward 0 and max_error to drop below 0.06 m, with progress rising on the oval and s-bend. The risk is that a wider array adds some oscillation, which the next race will show.
